name: Cadence canonical design system surface catalog
summary: A global inventory of design-system families across Cadence surfaces. This catalog defines the shared design contract; each surface can satisfy the contract with native implementation files for its runtime.
rules: Canonical families define visual language, state behavior, accessibility expectations, and product semantics; they do not require every surface to share the same source component.
Surface implementations should reuse shared tokens and primitives where practical, then adapt module code to the runtime only when the framework boundary requires it.
The authenticated web app manifest remains the strict live React/Next traceability inventory until other surfaces add native manifests or benches.
Marketing, desktop, and mobile entries may point to Astro templates, CSS, static captures, or planned implementation notes until those surfaces have their own native component inventories.

surfaces.name: Authenticated web app
surfaces.notes: Primary live harness today. It renders fixture-backed React components and verifies product usages through design-system.usage.json.

surfaces.name: Astro marketing site
surfaces.notes: Shares Cadence tokens, voice, square ledger marks, CTAs, sections, and product captures, but does not share the authenticated app shell or React component source.

surfaces.name: Desktop app
surfaces.notes: Proposal-track surface. It should reuse tokens and presentational patterns while avoiding Next server components and server actions.

surfaces.name: Mobile app
surfaces.notes: Proposal-track surface following the desktop local-first direction. Shared contracts should bias toward tokens, primitives, and presentational module specs.

componentFamilies.name: Foundations and tokens
componentFamilies.definition: Color, type, spacing, radius, border, motion, and flat ledger rules shared by every Cadence surface.
sharedContract: IBM Plex Sans typography
0px radius and no decorative shadow
Bleached background, Ash Line dividers, Monolith Blue completed/selected state, Rust Signal for explicit Not Completed or caution
Responsive structure without fluid product type

surfaceImplementations.notes: Tailwind v4 CSS variables and product classes are the current canonical token implementation.
Astro uses matching CSS variables and section vocabulary, with marketing-specific hero and route styles.
Carry over Tailwind tokens or generated token outputs when the desktop track starts.
Use the same token names and semantic meanings even if native platform values are generated.

componentFamilies.name: Text actions
componentFamilies.definition: The default Cadence action vocabulary: underlined text, square geometry, visible focus, and reserved filled surfaces only for selected/destructive/fixed priority actions.
sharedContract: Transparent background by default
Thin underline with non-reflowing hover emphasis
Primary, secondary, and Rust Signal danger variants share the same geometry
Visible focus outline
At least 44px tap target where the action is row-level or mobile-critical

surfaceImplementations.notes: Implemented through product-action, product-action-primary, product-action-secondary, product-action-danger, and timeline-status-action classes plus component-level status actions.
Implemented by .button, .button--primary, .inline-link, and CTA rows.
Should be a presentational primitive in the SPA/native shell.
Native implementation must preserve tap-target and focus/active affordance equivalents.

componentFamilies.name: Form controls
componentFamilies.definition: Square line-led inputs, selects, checkboxes, radio segments, and textareas used for behavior editing, settings, import/restore, and account deletion.
sharedContract: Use a single bottom Ash Line for default text inputs and selects
Use perimeter enclosure only when the control needs a clear functional boundary
Bleached background and Ink text
Readable disabled and error states
Native controls unless a custom control has a strong accessibility reason

surfaceImplementations.notes: Current field patterns are visible through behavior, settings, export, import, restore, and note fixtures. Behavior schedule controls use line-led fields; longer notes and confirmation fields keep functional enclosure.
Marketing has links and tables, but no launch-scope data-entry forms.
Use presentational form controls over local-first hooks/services.
Use native-friendly field sizing and platform keyboard behavior while preserving token semantics.

componentFamilies.name: Primary navigation
componentFamilies.definition: Top-level movement through each surface, using the same sparse ledger vocabulary but runtime-specific route structures.
sharedContract: Current route is visibly marked without decorative color
Routes stay few and named plainly
Mobile navigation remains reachable without hiding core actions

surfaceImplementations.notes: Fixed desktop rail and mobile drawer render from APP_NAV_ITEMS. The expanded Cadence brand mark/name links to Timeline with 70% opacity feedback, the collapsed desktop brand cell is an expand-only button that reveals the open-sidebar icon on hover, and the sticky mobile header fades in its bottom divider as the page scrolls.
Marketing header renders a Cadence-only brand lockup, Cadence and BehaviorLog route links, footer links including About, and a persistent login action.
Reuse the few-route structure, adapted to local-first shell constraints.
May use native/mobile navigation primitives but must preserve the same screen model.

componentFamilies.name: Surface shells
componentFamilies.definition: The structural shell around a surface: authenticated app shell, marketing document shell, and future desktop/mobile route shells.
sharedContract: Sections are unboxed or divided by quiet rules
No marketing-heavy composition inside the authenticated app
Bench or story surfaces are excluded from product usage counts

surfaceImplementations.notes: Authenticated shell owns app navigation, route framing, the Timeline banner, and the shared full-width decorative page banner for ScreenFrame-backed pages.
Static document shell owns marketing metadata, header, footer, and page-section rhythm.
The shell should be a client SPA shell without Next server assumptions.
Mobile shell may be native or webview, but should keep screen structure compact and task-first.

componentFamilies.name: Disclosure sections
componentFamilies.definition: Open/close sections and row detail drawers. The native summary element acts as the hide/show trigger button for progressive detail such as create behavior, edit behavior, occurrence details, status review, note correction, and agent-readable docs groups.
sharedContract: Use native disclosure semantics where possible
Use the product disclosure trigger class for summary controls so cursor, marker hiding, focus, and tap affordance stay consistent
Use the shared disclosure indicator where the section needs a visible opener; omit a separate icon when the row itself is the trigger
Keep the trigger-to-content spacing standardized through the disclosure pattern rather than one-off row padding
Do not hide primary occurrence decisions behind disclosure
Collapsed state should remain scannable and factual

surfaceImplementations.notes: Behavior creation, settings editing, archived behavior access, behavior date review, and Timeline row details use native details/summary. Timeline rows omit a separate disclosure icon by contract; the row summary itself is the trigger.
Marketing uses static sections and tables rather than app-style editable disclosures.
A shared presentational disclosure pattern is a good candidate for packages/ui later.
Disclosure must preserve mobile tap targets and avoid nested modal flows.

componentFamilies.name: First-run setup
componentFamilies.definition: Optional first-run setup that appears as a non-modal Timeline pop-up and routes into existing behavior, notification, timezone, and import controls.
sharedContract: Never requests notification permission on page load
Uses factual status labels without progress or reward language
Links into existing app controls rather than creating a separate wizard
Import stays optional and does not block setup completion

surfaceImplementations.notes: The Timeline route renders the setup pop-up only when the onboarding model says required setup remains.
Marketing explains the product but does not run authenticated setup.
Desktop setup should reuse the same completion semantics once that surface is scheduled.
Mobile setup may use native placement but must avoid a blocking wizard.

componentFamilies.name: Timeline feed
componentFamilies.definition: Current-day and future occurrence feed with compact occurrence rows, status decisions, details, and notes.
sharedContract: Current day leads the logged-in experience
Rows remain compact and unboxed
Completed, Not Completed, and Unresolved language stays exact
Occurrence notes attach to the occurrence, not the behavior

surfaceImplementations.notes: Live fixture-backed timeline module is rendered in the current bench.
Marketing uses sanitized static captures to communicate the same row vocabulary; the homepage uses the supplied exported hero image with the Timeline capture in the MacBook visual.
Likely reusable as presentational React components after removing server-action assumptions.
Mobile should preserve current mobile row structure and safe-area Needs decision action.

componentFamilies.name: Needs decision
componentFamilies.definition: The derived prior-day unresolved decision surface, including the fixed entry action and grouped decision modal/sheet.
sharedContract: Needs decision is derived, not a stored status
Use factual language and avoid missed/failure framing
Rows stay grouped by original local day
Resolved rows may remain correction-visible through the current local day

surfaceImplementations.notes: Implemented as fixed button plus modal/sheet with accessible dialog labeling.
Marketing references Needs decision through sanitized copy and captures only.
Reuse the derived-state contract through local services/resolvers.
Likely a native/full-height sheet equivalent with the same date grouping.

componentFamilies.name: Behavior review calendar
componentFamilies.definition: Completion-intensity heatmaps and behavior date review patterns on the Behaviors surface.
sharedContract: Unresolved never implies failure
Overall calendar uses completion share intensity
Behavior calendars expose day review only when there are occurrences
Cells remain square and state-readable without color alone

surfaceImplementations.notes: Live Behaviors fixture owns current heatmap and behavior date review behavior.
Marketing may describe analytics but does not render the live module.
Should be portable once resolver-fed view models are available in the local-first shell.
May need denser or horizontally scroll-free cell sizing while preserving status semantics.

componentFamilies.name: Settings controls
componentFamilies.definition: Settings panels for profile-adjacent account operations: timezone, browser notifications, trust/legal links, and account deletion.
sharedContract: Settings stays sparse and divider-led: a single-column stack with exactly one divider between adjacent sections, no per-section perimeter borders, and no nested container repeating a parent boundary
Timezone is chosen from one native select of IANA timezones whose value is the saved timezone; a detected-timezone hint appears only when it differs from the saved value
Permission prompts happen only from explicit user action
Timezone uses browser/OS data without geolocation
Account deletion requires export acknowledgement and typed confirmation

surfaceImplementations.notes: Settings modules are fixture-backed in the bench with bench-only actions for mutable controls.
Marketing links to the app and public account-information routes but does not render account settings.
Desktop settings should separate local storage concerns from hosted account controls.
Mobile settings should keep destructive account operations explicit and hard to trigger accidentally.

componentFamilies.name: Behavior editor
componentFamilies.definition: Behavior creation/editing, recurrence, schedule slots, reminders, archive/restore, and behavior list management.
sharedContract: Behavior is the recurring tracked object
Recurrence presets stay explicit; no natural language recurrence UI
Browser reminders default on, email reminders default off
Archive preserves history

surfaceImplementations.notes: Current live behavior management modules are fixture-backed in the bench.
Marketing explains behavior management but does not provide editing controls.
Should extract presentational pieces only after desktop work is scheduled.
Likely needs native-friendly slot editing while preserving recurrence semantics.

componentFamilies.name: Export and portability
componentFamilies.definition: Export downloads, BehaviorLog import/restore, Markdown summary, and marketing bundle/documentation captures.
sharedContract: Portability remains factual and inspectable
Downloads and restore/import actions must be explicit
Sensitive imports require acknowledgement
BehaviorLog files are presented as authoritative records, not marketing decoration

surfaceImplementations.notes: Current export/import/restore modules are in the web app manifest and bench.
Marketing renders BehaviorLog bundle captures, docs tables, and example download links.
Desktop import/export should bridge local storage and existing full JSON/BehaviorLog outputs.
Mobile export affordances may differ, but warnings and explicitness stay canonical.

componentFamilies.name: Brand marks
componentFamilies.definition: Cadence and BehaviorLog marks, lockups, and square ledger visual motifs.
sharedContract: Cadence remains the tracker brand object
BehaviorLog supports the standard/adoption narrative as the portability layer
Marks use square ledger cells, Ash Line strokes, and restrained fills

surfaceImplementations.notes: Web app uses the Cadence app mark and compact shell branding.

Marketing uses the Cadence mark and name in the header plus the supplied trajectory horse and MacBook capture image in the homepage hero; BehaviorLog is represented through page copy, bundle captures, and the BehaviorLog route.
Desktop app icon and shell branding should derive from this family.
Mobile app icon and splash/launch marks should derive from this family when scheduled.
